name: Dermal Pattern Induction
description: Programs melanocyte cells to produce permanent, complex patterns in the skin — geometric designs, text, images, or abstract art rendered in natural pigment rather than ink. Unlike traditional tattoos, geneprints are produced by the body itself and heal cleanly without scarring. Advanced versions from Lacuna Genomics can produce patterns that shift slowly over days or weeks, creating living art that evolves. The most expensive installations include bioluminescent elements that glow in darkness. Street clinics offer static geneprints for less than the cost of a meal. The technology has essentially replaced traditional tattooing in Meridian 88, though some purists insist on needle-and-ink work as a statement of authenticity. Geneprints can encode information — some residents carry their medical records, identity codes, or sentimental messages written in their skin.
source_organism: Danio rerio (zebrafish, pigment patterning genes), synthetic melanocyte modulators
manufacturer: Lacuna Genomics (premium shifting patterns), widespread street availability (static)
procedure: Topical retroviral application with stencil guidance, single session
expression_time: 1–2 weeks for static patterns; 4–6 weeks for shifting variants
reversibility: Reversible with melanocyte reset treatment; complex patterns may leave ghost images
side_effects: Shifting patterns may drift from intended design over years
Skin irritation at pattern boundaries during expression
Rare: pattern spreads beyond intended area in budget installations
social_perception: Universal. Geneprints have replaced tattoos entirely for most people. They're used for art, identity, medical data, gang marking, corporate branding, memorial, and fashion. A person without any geneprints is unusual.
story_hooks: A dead body's geneprints contain an encrypted message that only becomes readable when the bioluminescent elements are activated
A street artist discovers they can hack geneprint patterns through skin contact, overwriting other people's body art with their own designs
